name: GTA V Frame Tick
description: Per-frame composition: input, streaming, movement, then the draw.

steps.comment: quake3's input group, copied so the Tab map can free the cursor: it only produces move/look/jump/crouch intent, which the q3.pm.* steps consume.

Pins the player at the spawn point until the ground under them has streamed in -- read on demand, that takes seconds, and unheld the player falls through the empty world. After the physics group, so it overrides this frame's movement; before streaming, so streaming centres on the spawn point.

E at an LS Customs or an Ammu-Nation opens its menu: any car from data/garage.json parked on the nearest road, a respray, weapons from data/weapons.json, ammunition and armour. After the physics, as the hold is, since it keeps the player at the counter.
What the player holds and fires: the weapon wheel on Q or LB, the left button or RT to fire, R to reload, and rockets and grenades that fly and go off. After the shop, which hands the weapons over.
Streaming runs after movement so it centres on the origin this frame produced rather than the last one's.

Read from the map on the fly: the body from taxi_hi.yft, its axles from that fragment's wheel bones, and the wheel from vehiclemods/wheels_mods.rpf. Paint and wheel size stand in for carcols.ymt and vehicles.meta, which are not in the extract. On the Grand Senora Desert road, in-game (1119, 3490); y is only where the drop starts looking, since nothing out there is overhead. Downtown kept putting it on kerbs and in underpasses. Spawns once the ground under it has streamed in.
F gets in and out of the nearest car, WASD drives, space brakes. Forces land a frame later than they are pressed, since the physics step already ran this frame.

Chase camera while seated. After vehicles_sync so it reads this frame's chassis, and before render_prepare so it overrides the first-person view camera.fps.update wrote -- which, seated, is from inside the roof.
The clock: sun, moon and sky by the hour. Hold T to run it an hour a second.
What fills the water: water.xml's surface heights as a grid the shaders read, and how deep the camera is.

Footsteps, strokes and splashes, the engine of the car last driven, and the lapping shore. dir holds GTA's own sounds as WAVs, exported from its AWC banks, in steps/, strokes/, splash/, engine/ and water/; any folder left empty plays a synthesised stand-in. After water_map, which says how deep the camera is.

Into a car, a random station, tuned in mid-song. dir holds a folder of WAVs per station, exported from GTA's RADIO_* banks (x64/audio/sfx); names maps folder names to station names. With nothing exported, stand-in stations play.
The sun's shadow map: casters within radius metres of the camera, from the sun, into a size x size depth map.
What the sea mirrors: the sky and the reflection and water proxies seen from the camera reflected in sea level.
Renders into an HDR target rather than straight to the swapchain, at twice the window's size: the composite resolves it down with a light sharpen, which keeps distant detail sharp and still.

Before the tiles and at depth 1.0, so the city occludes it by depth test. Colours are linear: the composite applies ACES then gamma, which lifts them a long way. The horizon is also the city's fog colour -- the step publishes it -- so the two cannot drift into a band where the tiles run out.
GTA V's sea, lakes and rivers from water.xml (extracted from common.rpf with GTAUtil).
GTA's distant lights at night: far-off street lamps and lit windows from lodlights.rpf.
Muzzle flashes, tracers, the dust off a hit, fireballs, smoke and the scorch left behind: quads in world space, blended over the scene.
Blits the scene target to the swapchain. Without this and the submit below, the draws land in a texture nobody presents and the window stays black.
What gta5.player.hold is waiting on, in the overlay; a blank once the ground is in, so the label goes away.
The heads-up display: health and armour bars, the weapon and its ammunition, and while driving a speedometer and tachometer. Over the finished frame; the Tab map, after it, covers it.
Tab: GTA's pause-map art full screen, with an arrow where the player is. The rectangle is the world the six minimap tiles cover, in metres, GTA's y north.
